body.text:
Viv:
1. svavimarśavikacakānana&samunmiṣadviṣayakusumasaṃtatyā
karaṇeśvarībhir abhitaḥ & samarcito bodhabhairavo jayati
2. vimarśamayyā nijaśaktidevyā & viśvaprathābhairavakḷptapūjaḥ
jayaty akāmoditaraśmirūpa&svaśaktipuñjātmajacakranāthaḥ \var{puñjātmaja\lem puñjākara \kha}
3. kramākramakriyākrānti&vyatikramanikṛntanam
devaṃ cakraṃ śraye krīḍā&kroḍīkṛtakṛtāntakam
body.translated_text: [Commentary (<s>Vivṛti</s>):] 1. Victorious is <s>Bodhabhairava</s> (the <s>Bhairava</s> of Awakening), worshipped on all sides by the sovereign goddesses of the senses (<s>karaṇeśvarīs</s>), through the unbroken garland of sense-object flowers blossoming from the face [of consciousness] expanded by self-reflective awareness (<s>svavimarśa</s>). 2. Victorious is <s>Cakranātha</s> (Lord of the Wheel), the son of the mass of his own powers in the form of rays that bloom without [external] desire, whose worship is fashioned by <s>Bhairava</s> in the form of the expansion of the universe, through his own power-goddess (<s>śakti-devī</s>) consisting of reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>). 3. I take refuge in the god who is the Wheel (<s>Cakra</s>), who cuts through the transgression of the step-by-step progression and non-progression of action (<s>kramākrama-kriyā</s>), who has drawn the Ender of Death (<s>Kṛtānta</s>) into the lap of [his] play.

body.text: iha hi niruttaranirniketanāvaṭaviṭaṅkasaṃkalitasakalakalanākulaṃ paramabhairavacakreśvarasatatattvam avācyavācakam avarṇanirvarṇanam anādyanantam antarbahīrūpam apūjyapūjakam api prasaradādyodyantṛtāvatārakramāvatāritapañcavāhaprapañcamayākṛtrimapūjyapūjanakakrameṇa protsphurati iti rītir avigītasukhasaṃpradāyasaraṇisamanugatasarvāgamāntaraghumaghumāyamānaśrīvijñānabhairavādiṣu svakaṇṭhenaivabhagavatā nirṇītā, śrīsvatantrabhaṭṭārakādiṣu ca
body.translated_text: For here, the supreme reality of <s>Bhairavacakreśvara</s> (the Lord of the Wheel of <s>Bhairava</s>), which is unsurpassable, shelterless, pervaded by all the arts assembled in the hollow of [its] nest, [which is] the inexpressible-yet-expressed, the undescribable-yet-described, beginningless and endless, of both inner and outer form, the unworshipped-yet-worshipped — it nevertheless shines forth through the order of spontaneous worship of the worshippable, fashioned as the illusory play of the fivefold stream (<s>pañcavāha</s>) descending through the descending order of the initial arising and setting of expansion. This method has been definitively established by the <s>Bhagavān</s> himself in the <s>Śrī Vijñānabhairava</s> and other texts, which resound within all the <s>āgamas</s> that follow the path of the tradition of uncontested bliss, and also in the <s>Śrī Svatantrabhaṭṭāraka</s> and other [texts] —

body.text: Q: akṛtvā mānasaṃ yāgaṃ
body.translated_text: [Quotation:] 'Without performing the mental sacrifice (<s>mānasa-yāga</s>)'

body.text: ityādivākyair dhvanitā mānasayāgātirekiṇī sarvabhāvopahṛtiḥ, tām eva bhaṭṭārakapādāḥ stotramukhena prakaṭayanta ādiślokena āsūtrayanti
body.translated_text: — by such statements, the offering of all states of being (<s>sarvabhāvopahṛti</s>), which transcends mental sacrifice, is indicated. The revered master (<s>bhaṭṭārakapāda</s>), revealing precisely this through the medium of a hymn (<s>stotra</s>), summarizes [it] in the opening verse:

children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>
Homage to the one who steals away the body of Time through the net of solar rays (<s>sūrya-kalā-jāla</s>),
to the one who is the seat (<s>pīṭha</s>) of support and supported, to the one who is Existence (<s>bhava</s>) and who bestows Non-existence (<s>abhava</s>).

body.text: Viv: bhavāya helāmātrodbhāvitabhavābhavāya namaḥ / nama iti namaḥśabdagatavarṇadvayavityāsena (?) caturthyantapadāveditatatsvarūpasarvāvedananayena unmanībhāvaḥ tatsamāviṣṭena sūcitaḥ, tena tatra mano vilāpayāmīty arthaḥ / kāladehaṃ vā kālavikalpanollāsikāmīhaṃ vā sūryakalājālena dvādaśātmakamarīcicayena yo 'paharatīti tacchīlo 'yam akramapadena darśitaḥ, sūrīnāmakalājālena madhyamadhāmānuvedhena bhāvābhāvabhūmyullaṅghanātmanā kāladehāpahārī mahāhaṅkārātmakamahākāladeham apahartuṃ śīlaṃ yasya sa tathoktaḥ / tad uktaṃ
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] [Homage] to <s>Bhava</s> — to the one who, by mere play, manifests existence and non-existence. '<s>Namaḥ</s>' — through the dissolution of the two syllables contained in the word <s>namaḥ</s>, by the method of non-cognition of that very nature indicated by the word in the dative case, the state of <s>unmanī</s> (transcendent mind) is indicated as [being experienced] by one absorbed in that [state]; therefore the meaning is: 'I dissolve my mind in that.' Or: he who steals the body of Time — i.e., the desire (<s>kāmīha</s>) that gives rise to the play of temporal differentiation — through the net of solar rays (<s>sūrya-kalā-jāla</s>), the array of twelve-fold rays — this nature of his is shown by the word <s>akrama</s> (non-sequential). Or: through the net of rays of the suns (i.e., master-practitioners), by the piercing of the middle and lower [planes], he steals the body of <s>Mahākāla</s> (Great Time), constituted by the great ego (<s>mahāhaṅkāra</s>), in the form of transcending the planes of being and non-being — this is his nature, and he is so described. As stated —

body.text: Q: kālīṃ mahākālam alaṃgrasantīm
body.translated_text: [Quotation:] '<s>Kālī</s>, devouring <s>Mahākāla</s>'

body.text: ityādi / tataś ca sūryakalājālena vā sūryakalājālam eva vā kāladeham apaharatīty alaṃgrāsamahaughaḥ prakaṭitaḥ, na hy akramānākhyaparaciccakreśvarīsamudaye kālo nāma kaścid upapadyate / tad uktaṃ mayaivākramakallolakārikāsu
body.translated_text: — and so forth. Therefore, by means of the net of solar rays, or [by swallowing] the very net of solar rays which is the body of Time, he steals [it] — thus the great flood of total devouring (<s>alaṃgrāsa</s>) is revealed. For in the arising of the supreme Consciousness-Goddess (<s>cicchakti</s>-<s>eśvarī</s>) called <s>akrama</s> (the non-sequential), no such thing as 'Time' can exist. As stated by myself in the <s>Akramakallolakārikās</s> —

body.text:
Q: kālaḥ kālena kālyaś cet & kālaḥ kālyeta kena vā
akālya eva kālaś cet & kālya eva tathāḷna kim
mṛtyuḥ sphuratprakāśāntar&nigīrṇo nigiret katham
asphurann aprakāśatvān & nāntargrāhyo 'thavā na kim
body.translated_text: [Quotation:] 'If Time is to be devoured by Time, then by whom would Time be devoured? If Time is itself undevourable, then is it not [equally true that it is] devourable? Death, swallowed within the flashing light [of consciousness], how could it devour? And if it does not flash forth, then, being without illumination, it cannot be an inner object [of cognition] — is that not so?'

body.text: iti / tathādhārādheyau ṣaḍadhvataduttīrṇarūpau bhavābhavau tatsthyaivāsya, udyogāvabhāsacarvaṇavilāpanataduttarakṛtyayogāt pīṭha iva pīṭho yasya \pratika{ādhārādhyeyapīṭhāya} iti tu pāṭhe ādhāre dhyeyā śaktir eva tadadhiṣṭhānena sādhiṣṭhānatvāt pīṭho yasya tasmai bhavāya, abhavadāyine 'śivaparikhaṇḍanāya mokṣapradāya vā nama ity anena kāladehāpahāriṇādhārādheyapīṭhatvapratipādanena sarvātmasātkaraṇalakṣaṇaḥ satatodito 'kṛtrimapūjānaya uṭṭaṅkitaḥ / atrāpahāripadena saṃhāra uktaḥ, pīṭhapadena sthitikramah, bhavapadena sṛṣṭiḥ, ity akramaughaḥ sṛṣṭiparyavasānenānena ślokena carcitaḥ / caturthasya sakalakramākramabhittibhūtatvāt pṛthag anabhidhānam eva /
body.translated_text: Thus, the support (<s>ādhāra</s>) and the supported (<s>ādheya</s>) — the forms of the six paths (<s>ṣaḍadhvan</s>) and that which transcends them, [namely] being (<s>bhava</s>) and non-being (<s>abhava</s>) — these are his seat (<s>pīṭha</s>), because of the conjunction of the activities of arising (<s>udyoga</s>), illumination (<s>avabhāsa</s>), savoring (<s>carvaṇa</s>), dissolution (<s>vilāpana</s>), and the function that transcends those. In the reading '<s>ādhārādhyeyapīṭhāya</s>,' the <s>Śakti</s> (power) who is to be meditated upon in the support, by virtue of her being established in that [support], is his seat — [homage] to that <s>Bhava</s>, and to the bestower of <s>abhava</s>, the destroyer of the inauspicious, or the giver of liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>). By this [verse's] teaching that he is the stealer of the body of Time and has support-and-supported as his seat, the mode of worship consisting of total self-assimilation (<s>sarvātmasātkaraṇa</s>), which is perpetually arisen and spontaneous, is engraved. Here, by the word 'stealer' (<s>apahārin</s>), dissolution (<s>saṃhāra</s>) is indicated; by the word 'seat' (<s>pīṭha</s>), the order of maintenance (<s>sthiti</s>); by the word 'existence' (<s>bhava</s>), creation (<s>sṛṣṭi</s>) — thus the flood of the non-sequential (<s>akrama</s>) is discussed in this verse, ending with creation. The fourth [function], being the foundation of all sequential and non-sequential [processes], is not separately mentioned.

body.text: atha sthitipradhānasṛṣṭisaṃhāraparighaṭṭanena dvitīyaṃ pūjākramaṃ darśayati:
body.translated_text: Now, showing the second order of worship through the churning of creation and dissolution with maintenance as primary:

children.translated_text: Homage to the one who wears the garland of lotuses (<s>kalākamalas</s>) that are the digits of the child-moon (<s>śiśu-niśākānta</s>),
to <s>Śiva</s>, whose body is supreme bliss (<s>paramānanda</s>), whose form is unmanifest (<s>avyaktamūrti</s>).

body.text: Viv: avyaktā bhavābhavasthitiprādhānyād uṭṭaṅkatvenāprakaṭitā mūrtir yasya tasmai śivāya mahatyāveśe 'py aparibhraṃśaśīlāya / nama iti vyākhyātam / śiśutayādyā bhedasvabhāvena sthitā yeyaṃ niśākāntasya kālarātrīramaṇasya parabhairavasya kalanāt kalā saivāghoraghorāghorātighorāvaraṇatrayopetavargāṣṭakadalalālitā, saiva kamalaṃ tanmāline tadādhārāya tadādheyāya vā / niśākāntakalā saṃhāradevī, tathā cāsmatputraḥ
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Unmanifest' — whose form, due to the predominance of the state of being and non-being, is not manifested prominently — [homage] to that <s>Śiva</s>, whose nature is not to lose [his composure] even in great possession (<s>āveśa</s>). '<s>Namaḥ</s>' has been explained. The first [digit], standing in its nature as differentiation by virtue of being a child (<s>śiśu</s>), which is the <s>kalā</s> (digit/phase) of the Lord of the Night of Time (<s>kālarātri-ramaṇa</s>), [namely] <s>Parabhairava</s>, through her art of division — she, adorned with petals of eight groups endowed with three coverings of <s>Aghora</s>, <s>Ghorā</s>, and <s>Atighorā</s>, is herself the lotus, and [homage is] to the one who wears her as a garland — i.e., to her support or to her container. The digit of the moon-lord is the goddess of dissolution (<s>saṃhāra-devī</s>); and thus our son [says] —

body.text:
Q: śivaśivāsanamūrdhni sadā sthitā & vigatakālakalākalanākramā /
Q: kṛśatayā kraśimavyapalāpinī & jayati kāpi kalā vigatakramā
body.translated_text: [Quotation:] 'Always standing upon the head of the seat of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śivā</s>, free from the sequence of the art of the digit of Time, refuting thinness by her very thinness — victorious is a certain digit beyond sequence.'

body.text: iti / vājasaneyabhaṭṭārikāyām api
body.translated_text: And in the <s>Vājasaneyī Bhaṭṭārikā</s> also —

children.translated_text: [Quotation:] 'The <s>avadhūtā</s> (liberated one), beyond all observances, abiding within all beings,'

children.text: Q: krīḍaty ātmamayair bhāvair & bālaḥ krīḍanakair iva //
children.translated_text: [Quotation:] 'She plays with states of being made of herself, as a child [plays] with toys.'
[Quotation:] 'Dividing herself by herself through the two states of awakened and fully [awakened],'
[Quotation:] 'Through the unawakened and the awakened, she should intensely manifest [the universe] for the sake of play.'

body.text: iti / \pratika{māline} dhāriṇe iti sthitiḥ / \pratika{ānandadehāya} iti sṛṣṭis tasyā ānandarūpatvāt, \pratika{avyaktamūrtaye} iti saṃhāraḥ / ayam api satatasiddha eva pūjākramaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus. 'To the wearer of the garland (<s>māline</s>)' means: to the bearer — this is maintenance (<s>sthiti</s>). 'Whose body is bliss (<s>ānandadeha</s>)' — this is creation (<s>sṛṣṭi</s>), because her nature is bliss. 'Whose form is unmanifest (<s>avyaktamūrtaye</s>)' — this is dissolution (<s>saṃhāra</s>). This order of worship too is perpetually accomplished. //

body.text: atha guṇībhūtasṛṣṭisthitirūpatṛtīyacakrākramapūjāṃ pratijānīte
body.translated_text: Now he proposes the worship of the third wheel (<s>cakra</s>), the non-sequential (<s>akrama</s>) [worship], in which creation and maintenance have become subordinate [to dissolution]:

children.translated_text: Homage to the one who brings about the dissolution and separation of the mass of bonds (<s>pāśaugha</s>),
to <s>Hara</s> (the Destroyer), the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>), who abides in the womb-interior of <s>mantras</s> (<s>mantragarbhodara</s>).

body.text: Viv: pāśānām -- āṇavamāyīyakārmikāṇām malānām oghaḥ tasya saṃghaṭṭa ahetukena kenāpi krameṇa ullāsaḥ, tena vā tatra vā tasya vā yo 'yaṃ layaḥ, tathā viśleṣaḥ pṛthagbhāvas tatkaraṇaśīlatvena vartamānāya sadā tritayakāritvān nāntarīyakaṃ tirodhānānugrahakāritvaṃ dhvanitam / \pratika{mantragarbhodarasthāya} ity atra tridhā gurvāmnāyaḥ -- mantrā varṇarūpā garbhe yasyāḥ sā mālinī mantragarbhā tadantargatā tasyā udare vācyatvenābhyantare tiṣṭhatīti sa tathā, athavā mantrāṇāṃ garbho mantragarbhaḥ prathamasvaras tasyodaram uttarapakṣapratikṣepeṇa madhyamakalā tuṭyardharūpā tatra sthitā, athavā mananatrāṇadharmitvān marīciṣu sthityuditāsu mantra ityādirūpatayā yo 'yam anārāvarāvo rāvasaṃghaṭṭakatayā
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Of the bonds (<s>pāśa</s>) — the impurities (<s>mala</s>) that are <s>āṇava</s> (pertaining to the individual soul), <s>māyīya</s> (pertaining to <s>Māyā</s>), and <s>kārmika</s> (pertaining to <s>karma</s>) — the 'flood' (<s>ogha</s>) [means] the assemblage; 'collision' (<s>saṃghaṭṭa</s>) [means] the manifestation by some causeless sequence — and by that, or in that, or of that, the 'dissolution' (<s>laya</s>) and 'separation' (<s>viśleṣa</s>), i.e., differentiation — to the one whose nature is always to bring about [all] three, and therefore the capacity for concealment (<s>tirodhāna</s>) and grace (<s>anugraha</s>) is implied as inseparable. In the phrase 'who abides in the womb-interior of <s>mantras</s>,' the teacher's tradition is threefold: (1) <s>Mālinī</s> is she whose womb contains the <s>mantras</s> in the form of phonemes (<s>varṇas</s>) — she is the '<s>mantra</s>-womb'; he abides inside her, in her interior, as the expressed — thus he is so called. (2) Alternatively, the womb of <s>mantras</s> is the first vowel; its 'interior' (<s>udara</s>) is, by negation of the second option, the middle <s>kalā</s> in the form of half a <s>tuṭi</s>; he abides in that. (3) Or, because of having the nature of contemplation (<s>manana</s>) and protection (<s>trāṇa</s>), in the rays as they arise and abide, he who is this incessant reverberation in the form of '<s>mantra</s>' etc., by virtue of being the collision of reverberations —

body.text:
Q: tvām ajām akṛtapañcakāraṇa&drāvaṇoḍḍamaradhāmabhairavīm /
Q: staumy anāhatahatavyatikrama&sphārarāvakṛtavīraghaṭṭanām
body.translated_text: [Quotation:] 'I praise you, the Unborn One (<s>ajā</s>), the <s>Bhairavī</s> whose abode is the drumming and leaping [that] dissolve the un-created five causes, who creates the striking of heroes through the widespread reverberation of the unstruck-yet-struck transgression.'

body.text: ityādyasmadviracitākulakaulikātriṃśikoktasvarūpas tasya garbhaṃ gahanam avaṭarūpaṃ tadudare tadgamanikāgamye dhāmni tiṣṭhatīti sa tathoktaḥ, sarvatra cātrādyabhaṭṭārakopadeśa eva virājate tasyaiva paramātmatvāt, ata evātra bhavaśivaharaśabdaiḥ ślokatrayoditasṛṣṭyādyupadeśacaramasyānākhyasya sarvāntaścāritvam avāggocaratvāt sūcitam eva / atraughasaṃghaṭṭaśabdābhyāṃ sṛṣṭisthityoḥ, haraśabdena saṃhārasya dyotane 'kṛtakā kāpi pūjā nirūpitaiva //3
body.translated_text: — as described in the <s>Akulakaulikā Triṃśikā</s> composed by us — whose nature that is; of that, the 'womb' (<s>garbha</s>) is the depth, the hollow-form; he abides in its interior, in the abode accessible to its pathway — thus he is so called. And everywhere here, the teaching of the primordial master (<s>ādyabhaṭṭāraka</s>) alone shines forth, for he alone is the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>). Therefore, by the words <s>bhava</s>, <s>śiva</s>, and <s>hara</s> in the three verses, the fact that the fourth [state], the Unnameable (<s>anākhya</s>), which is the creation etc. taught in the final [verse], pervades all [the others], is indicated — since it is beyond speech. Here, by the words 'flood' (<s>ogha</s>) and 'collision' (<s>saṃghaṭṭa</s>), creation and maintenance are indicated; by the word '<s>Hara</s>' (Destroyer), dissolution — and thus a certain uncreated worship is established. // 3

body.text: tad evam anavacchinnasatatasiddhanirupādānānantanava_dhikasvarūpabhūtapūjāsaṃbhave śambhor nirguṇasyānantaguṇasya vopacārair anantair bāhyair vā kāyikair vācikair mānasair vā pūjayitum aśakyatvāt ko 'yaṃ bhāvopahāro nāma ity āśaṅkyāha
body.translated_text: Thus, since worship — which is the very nature of <s>Śambhu</s> (the Auspicious One), unconditioned, perpetually accomplished, without material cause, infinite, and ever-new — is possible [only as such], and since <s>Śambhu</s>, who is without qualities or of infinite qualities, cannot be worshipped by external observances — whether physical, verbal, or mental — however infinite, the question arises: 'What then is this so-called offering of states of being (<s>bhāvopahāra</s>)?' Anticipating this, he says —

children.text: yadyapi tvaṃ guṇātīto vākpater apy agocaraḥ
children.translated_text: Although you are beyond all qualities (<s>guṇātīta</s>), beyond even the reach of the Lord of Speech (<s>Vākpati</s>),

children.text: tathāpy ā hṛdayāt stotum udyatā vāk sadā mama
children.translated_text: nevertheless, my speech is always impelled to praise [you], from the [very depths of my] heart,
overwhelmed by the rush of the rasa (essence) of excessive devotion (<s>atibhaktirasāveśa</s>), O All-Faced One (<s>Viśvatomukha</s>) —

children.text: tvatpreritā yato nātha nāparādho 'sti me kvacit
children.translated_text: since [my speech] is impelled by you, O Lord, there is no offense on my part anywhere.

body.text: Viv: yadyapitathāpiśabdābhyām anupapattāv apy upapattiṃ prakāśayadbhyām anupapattir eva sarvopapattir iti kāpi yuktir uktā, tathā hi guṇātīto 'pi tasyaiva viṣayo 'pi tadullāsitena kenāpi durghaṭaghaṭanānayenārvācīnabhūmimūrtitvena viṣayadhāma aśnute / tad uktaṃ tapasviprabodhanāthena
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] By the words 'although' (<s>yadyapi</s>) and 'nevertheless' (<s>tathāpi</s>), which reveal possibility even in impossibility, a certain reasoning is stated: that impossibility itself is the ground of all possibility. For although he is beyond qualities, yet he is the very object [of praise]; and by some principle of accomplishing the impossible, brought forth by that [Lord] himself, descending as a form on the accessible plane, he attains the domain of objecthood. As stated by <s>Tapasviprabodhanātha</s> —

body.text:
Q: parataratayāpi rūpaṃ & yad yat kalayāmi tat tad adharaṃ te
Q: adharatarāpi na kalanā & sā kācid yatra na sthitāsy abhitaḥ /iti
body.translated_text: [Quoted verse:] Even [considering] the most transcendent form — whatever I perceive, all that is inferior to You. And even the most inferior perception — there is none in which You do not abide in every way.

body.text: ā hṛdayād ā paradhāmnaḥ paśyantyādirūpeṇa sadoditāpi vaikharyātmanā tvayaivaitenādyabhaṭṭārakena prakarṣeṇeritā satī prasarati, iti mam na kaś caid aparādha ity ahaṃ tatsamāveśita evoditaḥ, yady ahaṃ nāma kaś cid anyo bhaveyaṃ, bhaven nāma aparādho, yadi param aparādho 'py aham api bhavān apy ekam eva tattvaṃ, tataś ca ko 'parādhaśabdārthaḥ / tad uktaṃḷmayaiva śivaravastotre
body.translated_text: From the heart to the supreme abode, the [speech-power], though ever-arisen in the form of <s>Paśyantī</s> (the visionary level of speech), when fully impelled by You alone — this primordial Lord — in the form of <s>Vaikharī</s> (audible speech), she extends forth. Thus there is no fault of mine [in attempting to praise You]. For I have arisen as one pervaded by that [power] itself. If I were indeed someone other [than You], then there might be a fault. But even if there is a fault, I too and You too are one and the same <s>tattva</s> (reality) — and then what is the meaning of the word 'fault'? As has been stated by me in the <s>Śivaravastotra</s>:

body.text:
Q: atha vā hṛdambaragatena & janinidhanahīnamūrtinā
Q: candravimalamukuṭena nutāv & anumoditā mama matiḥ pravartate / iti
body.translated_text: [Quoted verse:] Or rather, by [<s>Śiva</s>] who resides in the space of the heart, whose form is free from birth and death, whose crown is pure as the moon — my thought, approved in [this] praise, proceeds forth.

body.text: atikrāntā bhaktirasāvibhāgabhūmir yena tādṛg yo 'yam āveśaḥ sarvatodikkatanmayatodayas tena vivaśā viśiṣṭā vaśeva kareṇur iva nijabodharasacarvaṇasadāvaraṇanirāvaraṇamadavighūrṇitatvād viśvataḥ sarvato mukhāni yasya sa tathā, ity anenaitad uktaṃ bhavati---na tad vācyaṃ kṛtyaṃ vā kiṃcana yat tvatparicarvaṇacārurūpatayā na cakāsti / tataś ca suptapralāpagālidānādibhir api tvam eva stūyase ity āha viśvato mukha iti visvata ā mukhaṃ yasyeti vā / paśukukkuṭādimūrtiparyantam asyāvirbhūtatvam abādhyam ity arthaḥ / sarvathāpy anuditān astamitāparimitacidekaghanam iti pratipāditam //4--5//
body.translated_text: The ground of devotional sentiment (<s>bhaktirasa</s>), whose [very nature is] non-differentiation, has been transcended by that [state of] absorption (<s>āveśa</s>) — an arising of identity with [the divine] in all directions. Being thereby overpowered — [yet] distinguished, like a she-elephant [in rut], due to being whirled about by the intoxication that constantly covers and uncovers the relishing of one's own awakening-essence (<s>bodharasa</s>) — [the divine is] 'whose faces are everywhere' (<s>viśvatomukha</s>). By this it is stated: There is nothing to be said or done that does not shine forth in the beautiful form of Your worship. Therefore, even through utterances in sleep, gifts given inattentively, and the like, You alone are praised — hence 'whose faces are everywhere' — or alternatively, 'whose face reaches everywhere.' The meaning is that His manifestation, extending even to the forms of animals, roosters, and the like, is unobstructable. In every way, [He is] the dense mass of consciousness (<s>cit</s>) alone — unarisen, unset, unlimited — thus it has been demonstrated. // 4-5 //

children.translated_text: Purified by the dust of Your lotus-feet, adorned with the glory of the funeral pyre (<s>citā</s>),
accept from me, O <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s> (Beautiful-Throated One), this offering of inner worship (<s>bhāvapūjā</s>), unartificial.

body.text: Viv: śrīr viśvavaicitryaśobhodhāvinī śaktiḥ kaṇṭhe 'vibhāgadhāmni yasya tasyāmantraṇaṃ, `gṛhāṇa' iti saṃpradānasaṃpradeyatayā tvam eva sphurasīti yāñcārthā akṛtktrimaśabdena sūcitā / tava pādāḥ piṇḍasthādibhedena catasro 'vasthās tā evābjaṃ tatra tadullāsitajñeyakāryavastu vikalparūpaṃ, rañjanād rajas tena pūtā tato vā pūtā sadyuktiparipavanena kṣapitā yā citābhūtiḥ sarvasaṃkṣayaparacidrūpā sarvodbhūtirūpā vā tayā viśiṣṭāyāṃ bhuvy uṣitāt prastoṣyamāṇān matto mama sakāśāt tvam api matto nijānandanirbharo bhāvapūjām ātasātkaroṣīti //6//
body.translated_text: Commentary: <s>Śrī</s> (the power of universal variegated beauty) resides at the 'throat' (<s>kaṇṭha</s>) — the undivided abode — of Him who is thus addressed. 'Accept' — the fact that You alone shine forth as both the recipient and the gift indicates the supplicatory meaning, suggested by the word 'unartificial.' Your 'feet' (<s>pāda</s>) are the four stages beginning with <s>piṇḍastha</s>; these themselves are the 'lotus' (<s>abja</s>); there, the knowable object-reality illuminated by them, in the form of conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>), is the 'dust' (<s>rajas</s>) — by which [one is] 'purified,' or 'purified' through the removal [of impurity] by proper reasoning. The 'glory of the funeral pyre' (<s>citābhūti</s>) is the consciousness-form (<s>cidrūpa</s>) that is the complete dissolution of all [duality], or the form of the arising of everything. From me, thus distinguished by that [glory], dwelling on that ground — and also 'from me' meaning 'intoxicated,' overflowing with one's own bliss — You accept this offering of inner worship. // 6 //

body.text: tām eva snānakrameṇa prastauti
body.translated_text: He praises that very [worship] in the sequence of bathing (<s>snāna</s>):

children.translated_text: Having bathed inwardly at the sacred ford (<s>tīrtha</s>) called the 'heart-lotus' (<s>hṛtpuṣkara</s>), frequented by <s>yoginīs</s>,
with the garment washed by awakening (<s>saṃbodha</s>), I worship the Dark-Throated One (<s>Śyāmakaṇṭha</s>).

body.text:
Viv: hṛtpuṣkaraṃ hṛtpadmaṃ tatra baddhalakṣyatayā snātvā sakalamalavidhūnananaṃ vidhāya, athavā haratīti hṛt saṃhārasaṃhāriṇīrūpam, etad eva hṛtpuṣkaraṃ tīrthaṃ sarvacakrāṇāṃ tatraiva paramaviśrāntilābhāt, tatra sarvaviśuddhim ādāya yogino 'tra pararaśmirūpāḥ, samyag bodhaḥ saṃbodhas tad eva dhautaṃ sakalakālikāviśuddhaṃ vasanam aśeṣācchādakatayā vartamānam yasya, iti sarvottīrṇasarvamayatoktiḥ, śyāmakaṇṭhaḥ sarvaghaṭṭakamahātamisrārūpasaṃkalanadhāmātmikā śyāmā kaṇṭhe gale yasya / yathoktam
Q: pānāśanaprasādhana&saṃbhuktasamastaviśvayā śivayā
Q: pralayotsavasarabhasayā & dṛḍham upagūḍhaṃ śivaṃ vande
body.translated_text: Commentary: The 'heart-lotus' (<s>hṛtpadma</s>) — having bathed there, i.e., having fixed one's attention there and performed the complete shaking off of all impurities. Or: <s>hṛt</s> means 'that which carries away' — the form of the destroyer of dissolution; this very 'heart-lotus' is the sacred ford, because all the <s>cakras</s> (centers) find their supreme rest therein. The <s>yogins</s> (practitioners), who are of the nature of supreme radiance, reside there. True awakening (<s>samyagbodha</s>) is <s>saṃbodha</s>; that itself is the 'washed' garment — purified of all impurities, functioning as the complete covering [of reality]. [He is] 'Dark-Throated' (<s>Śyāmakaṇṭha</s>) — <s>Śyāmā</s> is the <s>Śakti</s> (power) who arises from the abode of immovable summit-reality, whose essence is the domain of combining all [forms of] the great darkness of universal contact, and she is at the 'throat' (<s>kaṇṭha</s>). As it is said: [Quoted verse:] 'I praise <s>Śiva</s>, tightly embraced by <s>Śivā</s> (the goddess), who with zeal for the festival of dissolution has consumed and enjoyed the entire universe in eating and drinking and adorning.' // 7 //
Thus. // 7 //

body.text: arghapātram āha---
body.translated_text: He states the <s>arghya</s> (offering-vessel):

children.translated_text: With the blood born from beings arisen in the Lord (<s>Prabhū</s>), the offering-vessel (<s>arghabhājana</s>)
is fashioned in the skull-bowl (<s>kandale</s>) of the body-skeleton of <s>Mahākāla</s> (Great Time), for You.

body.text: Viv: prabhau vyāpake bhairavadhāmny ūtāny anusyūtāni yāni bhūtāni pañcātmakaśaktivivartabhūtāni pṛthivyādīni, tatra saṃbhūtāni yāni śoṇitāni tatsvarūpavigalanasamuditacidrasarūpāṇi, tair arghabhājanaṃ mahāvimarśamayapūjanapātram ekaśaktiśuktivigalanarūpaṃ sarveṣām avikalpabhūmyadhirohavidāritavikalpamayamahākālakalevarakaraṅkakapāle kalāsaṃkarṣiṇīdhāmamadhye vidhīyata ity alaṃ rahasyodghāṭanena //8//
body.translated_text: Commentary: In the Lord (<s>Prabhū</s>), the all-pervading <s>Bhairava</s>-abode, are woven the elements (<s>bhūta</s>) — the fivefold power-transformations beginning with earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>). The 'blood' (<s>śoṇita</s>) born therein is the consciousness-essence (<s>cidrasa</s>) that has arisen from the melting of their essential nature. By these, the offering-vessel — a vessel of worship composed of the great reflective awareness (<s>mahāvimarśa</s>), in the form of the melting of the singular <s>Śakti</s>'s shell — is fashioned in the skull-cup (<s>kapāla</s>) of the skeleton-body of <s>Mahākāla</s>, whose <s>vikalpa</s>-constituted [nature] has been split open by the ascent to the undifferentiated ground — in the domain of the power that draws together all the <s>kalās</s> (phases). Enough of revealing secrets! // 8 //

children.translated_text: Whatever network of conceptual construction (<s>vikalpanājāla</s>) [arises] for the apprehension of external objects,

children.text: tat tad dvārādhipakulaṃ tava pūjyaṃ manasvibhiḥ
children.translated_text: that very [network] is the assembly of doorkeepers (<s>dvārādhipakula</s>) — to be worshipped by the wise, O Lord.

body.text: Viv: bāhyaviṣayākṣepakatvān manonmanālakṣaṇaṃ dvāraṃ tadvāsi kulaṃ dvāḥsthakulaṃ dvāḥsthasamūhaḥ, vikalparasā eva hi svarūparasāveśadravaṇenāsamvibhaktā bāhyakaṣyāsu kṣipanti, tad anu caivaṃ mānitās te svarūpanarapatisamīpam arpayanti, iti svaśaktibhāgāvadhānena pūjyaṃ svīkṛtamanaskaiḥ //9//
body.translated_text: Commentary: Because they cast [consciousness] toward external objects, [the doorway is] characterized by the <s>manonmanā</s> (beyond-mind) state — the 'door' (<s>dvāra</s>). Those who guard it are the 'doorkeeper assembly' — the group of doorkeepers. For the essences of conceptual construction (<s>vikalparasa</s>), being undivided through the melting of immersion in one's own essential flavor (<s>svarūparasa</s>), cast [consciousness] into external domains. And subsequently, being thus honored, they deliver [one] into the proximity of the sovereign of one's own nature. [This is] to be worshipped by those of focused mind, through attention to the portion of one's own <s>Śakti</s>. // 9 //

children.translated_text: In the <s>maṇḍala</s> (circle) of the hidden deep-sleep [state], freed from all coverings,
You are worshipped, O Beloved of the Mountain-born (<s>Nagajākānta</s>), in the eclipse (<s>grahaṇa</s>) of moon and sun!

body.text: Viv: camanād abāhyatvenāntar eva cimicimāyamānatvāt, dravaṇāc ca bahirlokayātrātmanā prasaraṇāt, tathā suṣṭhu ūraṇād iti candraśabdena sūryaśabdena ca jāgratsvapnayor grahaṇam, tayor grahaṇe ātmasātkaraṇe sati, aśeṣāvaraṇaiḥ sarvopādhibhiḥ, unmukte guuptasauṣuptamaṇḍale guptaṃ tirohitaṃ sauṣuptaṃ maṇḍalaṃ yatra tasmin turīye dhāmni, nagajā avicalakūṭasthadhāmasamullasitā śaktiḥ tasyāḥ kānta viśrāntadhāman, pūjyase satataṃ saṃbodhanenānubhūyase //10//
body.translated_text: Commentary: Through 'tasting' (<s>camana</s>) — because of internally vibrating as non-external; and through 'flowing' (<s>dravaṇa</s>) — because of extending outward as worldly activity: by the word 'moon' (<s>candra</s>) and the word 'sun' (<s>sūrya</s>) the states of waking and dreaming are indicated. In the 'eclipse' (<s>grahaṇa</s>) of those two — i.e., their absorption into oneself — the 'hidden deep-sleep <s>maṇḍala</s>' is the <s>turīya</s> (fourth) state, where the deep-sleep circle is concealed; 'freed from all coverings' means freed from all limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhis</s>). The 'Mountain-born' (<s>Nagajā</s>) is the <s>Śakti</s> arisen from the unmoving summit-abode; You are Her 'Beloved' (<s>Kānta</s>), the abode of repose. You are worshipped — constantly experienced through awakening. // 10 //

children.translated_text: Free from the confusion of acceptance and rejection, arising and undertaking, being and non-being,
the seat (<s>āsana</s>) is [that which has] its ground in pure awareness (<s>jñaptimātra</s>) alone, O Lord of the three worlds!

body.text: Viv: tyāgagrahodgamakriyābhāvābhāvavikalpanirmuktam ata eva mātṛmānameyollaṅghanena pramitimātraṃ nirviśeṣeṇa phalarūpam āsanam upalakṣaṇatayā tasyāpi sāpekṣatvāt tad apy ullaṅghitavato 'vyapadeśyasya tava, te nivedyata iti pāṭhe nivedyate niḥśeṣeṇa vedyate tadbhāvenānubhūyate, trijagato mātṛmānameyalakṣaṇasyādhiṣṭhātaḥ! hānādānādipadārthaṣaṭkanirdeśatvānapekṣam āsanaṃ sūcitam //11//
body.translated_text: Commentary: Free from the conceptual constructions of renunciation, grasping, emergence, and action, being and non-being — and therefore, having transcended the triad of knower, knowing, and known (<s>mātṛ-māna-meya</s>), the result (<s>phala</s>) which is pure awareness without distinction is the 'seat'; by way of indication, even that [is to be transcended], since it too is relational — for You who have transcended even that, who are beyond designation. In the reading 'is offered' (<s>nivedyate</s>), it means 'is completely known,' i.e., experienced by becoming that. O ruler of the three worlds characterized by knower, knowing, and known! A seat independent of the sixfold categories beginning with acceptance and rejection has been indicated. // 11 //

children.translated_text: The gift of a form (<s>mūrtidāna</s>), nourished by the radiance of <s>Śakti</s> that is free from [external] appearance,
having its ground in the seat of the <s>turīya</s> (fourth state) — I offer [it], O Lord of the world!

body.text: Viv: upabṛṃhitam upabṛṃhaṇam, bāhyārthāvabhāsarahitān avachinnacamatkārasāraśaktyavabhāsarūpaṃ, mūrter mūrcchitasatattvasya kiṃciducchūnatātmanaḥ pāripūrṇyollekhasya dānaṃ, vitarāmi vimṛśāmi, pūrṇāhantayā ca paradaniviṣṭam //12
body.translated_text: Commentary: 'Nourished' means 'nourishment' — the form of the radiance of <s>Śakti</s> whose essence is unbroken wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>), free from the appearance of external objects. The 'gift of a form' is the gift [offered] of that which has solidified into true reality, whose nature is a slight swelling-up, an intimation of fullness. 'I offer' means 'I reflectively contemplate' — and, established as the perfect I-consciousness (<s>pūrṇāhantā</s>), it is deposited in the supreme [reality]. // 12 //

children.translated_text: For one whose mind is free from the stain of the reckoning of direction, time, and place —
what wise person would perform invocation or dismissal of <s>Sthāṇu</s> (the Immovable One, <s>Śiva</s>)?

body.text: Viv: sthāṇor sthāsnor apracalitasarvagatacinmātravapuṣaḥ pṛthag digdeśakālaparigaṇanakalpanābhāvād āhvānopakramaṃ visarjanam avagatatattvah kaḥ karoti, vyatiriktadeśakālasaṃbhave hi kasya cid ānayanaṃ kutra cit prahāṇaṃ saṃbhāvyeta, iha tu sarvasyaiva tanmayatvāt kasyāhvānaṃ kuta āhvānaṃ, kasya visarjanaṃ kutra ca visarjanam iti tatsamāveśenaiva sarvasaṃsaktir uktā //13//
body.translated_text: Commentary: Of <s>Sthāṇu</s> — the Immovable One, whose body is pure consciousness (<s>cinmātra</s>), all-pervading, never departing — because there is no conceptual construction of separately reckoning direction, place, and time, what person who has understood the truth would perform an invocation or a dismissal? For the bringing of someone [to a place] and the sending away [from a place] would be conceivable only if separate place and time existed. But here, since everything is of His nature, whose invocation? From where the invocation? Whose dismissal? And to where the dismissal? — thus, through immersion in that [reality] itself, complete interconnection with everything is declared. // 13 //

children.translated_text: Having churned the ocean of <s>Śakti</s> with the two eyes — the sun and the moon —
I offer the anointing (<s>abhyaṅga</s>) with the nectar-essence of supreme [consciousness] (<s>parāmṛtarasa</s>) to <s>Śiva</s>.

body.text: Viv: abhyajyate 'nabhivyaktam aoi vyaktim ānīyate sṛṣṭikramāvadyotitā yena so 'bhaṅga upasnehakaḥ, netre prathamasūtre 'pi //14//
body.translated_text: Commentary: That by which [things] are anointed — i.e., the unmanifest is brought into manifestation, illuminated by the process of creation — is the 'anointing' (<s>abhyaṅga</s>), the applying of oil. The 'eyes' are [explained] in the first <s>sūtra</s> as well. // 14 //

children.translated_text: In the sense-organs, in the objects of the senses — which are accompanied by passion (<s>rāga</s>) and greed (<s>lobha</s>) —

children.text: niḥsnehatvaṃ prabhutvaṃ ca rūkṣam udvartanaṃ tava
children.translated_text: detachment (<s>niḥsnehatva</s>) and mastery (<s>prabhutva</s>) — that is Your dry rubbing (<s>rūkṣa udvartana</s>).

body.text: Viv: indriyārtheṣu śabdasparśarūparasagandheṣu viṣayabhūteṣu, indriyeṣu rāgalobhānuyāyiṣu satsv iti vyadhikaraṇe saptamyau, niḥsnehatvaṃ prabhutvaṃ cātyantāyuktir anabhiṣvaṅgas tadadhiṣṭhātṛtvena vā sphuraṇam
body.translated_text: Commentary: In the objects of the senses — sound, touch, form, taste, and smell — which are of the nature of objects; and in the sense-organs which are accompanied by passion and greed — these being in different grammatical cases (locatives). 'Detachment' (<s>niḥsnehatva</s>) and 'mastery' (<s>prabhutva</s>) — complete non-attachment, absence of clinging, or radiance as the presiding lord thereof.

body.text: Q: buddhavat sarvarāgī syāt & sarvadveṣyo 'tha bhairavaḥ
body.translated_text: [Quoted verse:] 'Like a <s>Buddha</s>, one should be passionately attached to all; and wrathful toward all, like <s>Bhairava</s>.'

body.text: iti nyāyenodvartanam aśeṣavāsanonmūlanam //15//
body.translated_text: In accordance with this principle, 'rubbing' (<s>udvartana</s>) is the complete uprooting of all latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>). // 15 //

children.translated_text: Having purified the sacred ford of <s>Bindu</s> (the point of consciousness) directly, through the impure [residue that is] not yet clear,
the bath of the essence of cessation (<s>virāmarasa</s>) should be offered to the One whose crest is the half-moon (<s>Candrārdhamauli</s>).

body.text: Viv: mahānādādyakalāvacūlāya ṣoḍaśasvararūpakalākalāpārambhādyavarṇarūpaśiroṅkuśarūpayā+ anacchakalayā baindhavaṃ tīrtham ubhayaśūnyabilarūpaṃ saṃśodhya nirgranthibandhaṃ vidhāya, nirodhanādanādāntavartiparamatṛptitālakṣaṇarasena kāryam abhiṣecanam //16//
body.translated_text: Commentary (<s>Vivṛti</s>): Having purified the <s>bindu</s>-<s>tīrtha</s> (sacred point), which has the form of the void-aperture of both [channels], by means of the formless <s>kalā</s> (phase) — beginning with the <s>kalā</s> in the form of the great resonance (<s>mahānāda</s>) etc., the cluster of <s>kalās</s> in the form of the sixteen vowels (<s>svara</s>), and the initial letter (<s>varṇa</s>) in the form of a cranial hook — having made an untying of the knots (<s>nirgranthihandha</s>), the consecration (<s>abhiṣecana</s>) should be performed with the essence (<s>rasa</s>) characterized by the supreme satisfaction (<s>paramatṛpti</s>) that abides within the <s>nāda</s> (resonance) and cessation (<s>nirodha</s>). //16//

children.translated_text: Having applied the rubbing of a cloth — the vast [garment] of the sky of self-awakening (<s>svaprabodha</s>), blossoming open —
we offer forth the transformations of your consciousness (<s>saṃvid</s>). [//17//]

body.text: Viv: svaprabodhaḥ svavimarśa eva+ ambaram anāvaraṇatvād vyoma ata evodāram udbhaṭaṃ vikasat sarvātmatayā prasarat sollāsitakāryācchādakatayā vastraṃ tena gharṣaṇaṃ pratyāvṛttinayena svāvadhānaṃ vidhāya, prāpte mahāsāmarasye, vigaliteṣu dvaitodayamahāsaṃtrāsaḍambhareṣv akhaṇḍitasvāvabodhanirmatsarabalīn sarvatodikkaṃ kṣipāmaḥ //17//
body.translated_text: Commentary (<s>Vivṛti</s>): Self-awakening (<s>svaprabodha</s>) is self-reflective awareness (<s>svavimarśa</s>) itself. Sky (<s>ambara</s>), because of its non-concealing nature — hence vast, sublime, blossoming open, i.e. spreading as the totality of all selves — the cloth [serves] as the covering of the joyfully effected result. By its rubbing — through the method of turning back [upon oneself], establishing self-attention (<s>svāvadhāna</s>): when the great equanimity (<s>mahāsāmarasya</s>) is attained, when the great terrors and pretenses of dualistic arising have dissolved, we cast in all directions the generous offerings (<s>balī</s>) of unbroken self-awareness, free from jealousy. //17//

children.translated_text: Flowing from the mountain-waterfall of the abandonment of both knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) and the knowable (<s>jñeya</s>),
granting supreme bliss (<s>paramānanda</s>), within me — this is your foot-washing water (<s>pādya</s>), limpid and clear. [//18//]

body.text: Viv: ubhayor api sāpekṣatvenānupapadyamānasvarūpatvāj jaḍājaḍayos triṣv api kāleṣu cidatirekeṇābhāva evāgamanād avicalatvān nagaḥ tatra yo nirjharo nirgato jharo vayohānirūpaḥ kālo yasmāt tādṛksvarūpaṃ tataḥ pravṛttaṃ paracamatkārarūpaṃ pādyaṃ
body.translated_text: Commentary (<s>Vivṛti</s>): Because the nature of both [knowledge and knowable] is unestablished due to their mutual dependence, and because of the non-existence of the inert and the non-inert in all three times apart from consciousness (<s>cit</s>), and because of their unwavering arrival — [they are like] a mountain (<s>naga</s>). The waterfall (<s>nirjhara</s>) therein — <s>jhara</s> having the form of the decay of age (<s>vayohāni</s>), from which flows that nature — the foot-washing water (<s>pādya</s>) in the form of wonder at the other,

body.text: Q: jhṝṣ-vayohānau
body.translated_text: Quotation: '<s>jhṝṣ</s> — [the root meaning] decay of age (<s>vayohāni</s>)' —

body.text: ity asya jhara iti rūpam
body.translated_text: its form is <s>jhara</s>.

body.text: Q: ṛdorap //18//
body.translated_text: Quotation: '<s>ṛdorap</s>' [grammatical rule]. //18//

children.translated_text: From the cave of the palace of vibration (<s>spanda</s>), [which is] abundant with the overflow of intense bliss (<s>ānanda</s>),
accept, O All-pervading Lord (<s>Vibhu</s>), the sipping water (<s>ācamana</s>) dripping with the water of absolute freedom (<s>kaivalya</s>). [//19//]

body.text: Viv: guṇādispandaniḥṣyaniṣu yat sāmānyaspandarūpam akramaprakaṭitanimeṣonmeṣasrṣṭisthitiprakāram īṣaducchūnatayā kiṃciccalanātmakam api tad eva mandiraṃ sarvasya prathamanivāsitvād amando 'navacchinna ānandaniḥṣyando 'ham ity ullekhacamatkāraprasaro yatra tādṛśaspandamandirasya kandarād agādhād dhāmnaḥ, unmiṣadananyatvarasarūpam ācamanaṃ gṛhāṇa kaivalyarasam api saṃhara, iti ko 'pi bandhamokṣottīrṇo naya unmīlitaḥ, ``mandarakandarāt'' iti vā pāṭhaḥ //19//
body.translated_text: Commentary (<s>Vivṛti</s>): That which is the general vibration (<s>spanda</s>) among the overflows of the vibrations of qualities etc. — the form of the non-sequential manifestation of creation and dissolution as the closing and opening [of the eyes], slightly swelling, having the nature of subtle movement — that itself is the palace (<s>mandira</s>), because it is the first abode of all. The overflow of uninterrupted bliss (<s>ānanda</s>), intense — is the flash of the wonder of the apprehension 'I am.' From the cave of such a palace of vibration — from the unfathomable abode — accept the sipping water, which has the form of the essence of the emerging non-otherness; absorb even the essence of <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation). Thus some method transcending both bondage and liberation is revealed. [Alternative reading: '<s>mandarakandarāt</s>' — 'from the cave of <s>Mandara</s> mountain.'] //19//

children.translated_text: Having washed the priceless pearl of the five knots (<s>granthipañcaka</s>) with the waters of concentration (<s>dhāraṇā</s>),
I offer the invaluable guest-water (<s>argha</s>) at your feet, O <s>Vṛṣākapi</s> (Bull-Monkey, epithet of <s>Śiva</s>). [//20//]

body.text: Viv: he vṛṣa svaśaktirasavarṣanapravaṇa! tathā+ akape acapala---kūṭastha! granthipañcakam indhikā+dīpikā+rocikā+mocikā+ūrdhvagālakṣaṇaṃ, manograthanād dhāraṇā vāruṇyādyā deśabandharūpāś cittasya tā evāmbhāsi tair aṣṭottaraśatasaṃkhyātāntikamukhyasaṃpradāyasiddhibhūmikolaṅghanakrameṇa+ amalatām āsādya, anarghyamūlyam---atulyatvāt//20//
body.translated_text: Commentary (<s>Vivṛti</s>): O <s>Vṛṣa</s> — one inclined to rain down the essence of one's own power (<s>śakti</s>)! And <s>akapa</s> — not fickle, immovable (<s>kūṭastha</s>)! The five knots (<s>granthipañcaka</s>) are characterized as: <s>indhikā</s> (kindling), <s>dīpikā</s> (illuminating), <s>rocikā</s> (relishing), <s>mocikā</s> (liberating), and <s>ūrdhvagā</s> (ascending). <s>Dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) — because of the binding of the mind — is the <s>Vāruṇī</s> etc., having the form of localized bindings of consciousness; those very ones are the waters. By these, through the sequence of traversing the stages of attainment of the primary and ultimate lineage-traditions numbering one hundred and eight, having arrived at purity — [the offering is] of priceless value, because of its incomparability. //20//

children.translated_text: With the fragrance of consciousness (<s>saṃvit</s>) blossoming in the garden of the Fourth State (<s>turīya</s>), fully saturated,
O Lord of the Mountain (<s>Girīśa</s>), by the three [levels of] speech (<s>vāk</s>), with flowers of praise (<s>stuti</s>), you are worshipped. [//21//]

body.text: Viv: giri vāgviṣaye īśa svāmin, turīyodyāne parāsvarūpakānane vikasad yad etat saṃvitsaurabhaṃ bodhāmodas tannirbharaiḥ, stutirūpaiḥ puṣpaiḥ, tisṛbhir vāgbhiḥ pūjyase / tatra paśyantyāḥ tāvat svarūpāvyatiriktāntāsphuṭatedantāhantāvabhāsaparamasāmarasyarūpā stutiḥ, madhyamāyā api grāhyagrāhakākalpakalpanānalpasphurattātātparyaparyavasito 'py aviluptasvāvabhāsas tava stavastabakaḥ, vaikharyās tu maukharyeṇa sphuṭaghaṭapaṭādinaṭanalāmpaṭye 'pi sarvatodikkaprathitaparameśvararūpātirekivācyāntaravirahāt satatam eva tadanuśaṃsaiva kusumitā mitābhidhānanirṇayanirdalanatātparyaparyavasitā ityuktaṃ bhavati //21//
body.translated_text: Commentary (<s>Vivṛti</s>): O <s>Girīśa</s> — lord (<s>īśa</s>) in the domain of speech (<s>giri</s>)! In the garden of <s>turīya</s> (the Fourth State), in the grove of the <s>Parā</s> (Supreme [Speech]) nature, the blossoming fragrance of consciousness (<s>saṃvit</s>) — the aroma of awakening (<s>bodha</s>) — fully saturated with that; with flowers in the form of praise (<s>stuti</s>), by the three [levels of] speech, you are worshipped. Of these: the praise of <s>Paśyantī</s> (the Seeing [Speech]) has the form of the supreme equanimity (<s>sāmarasya</s>) of the not-clearly-manifest appearance of 'this,' 'I,' and the perceiver, which is not different from one's own nature. Of <s>Madhyamā</s> (the Middle [Speech]) also — the cluster of your praise concludes in the purport of the abundant flashing of non-conceptual construction of grasper and grasped, yet without loss of self-awareness. Of <s>Vaikharī</s> (the Corporeal [Speech]), however — even in the eagerness of the dramatic dance of clearly manifest pots, cloths, etc., because of the absence of any expressible other than the nature of the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>) pervading all directions, it is always an extolling of That alone; it culminates in the intent of splitting open the determination of limited designation — thus it is stated. //21//

children.translated_text: Having pierced the shining <s>Brahma</s>-aperture (<s>brahmabila</s>) with the weapon of the flame of the <s>prāṇa</s>-fire,
the radiance resembling the coil of incense — [this is] your incense (<s>dhūpa</s>), O Husband of the Mountain's Daughter (<s>Nagajādhava</s>). [//22//]

body.text: Viv: prāṇoddīpitā yeyaṃ vahniśikhā---āgneyadhāmakoṭiḥ, saiva astāt trāyate iti astraṃ, atha vā niṣkalanātho 'tra udvṛttaḥ, tenaiva hikkāpātoddīpitena granthibhedanakrameṇa brahmagranthibhedāt, tatra prāṇo ``ha'' vahniśikhārūpam astram ityādi, sarvaprameyajātaṃ dhūpayati sarvaṃ svaṃparispandenādhivāsayatīti dhūpaḥ //22//
body.translated_text: Commentary (<s>Vivṛti</s>): The <s>prāṇa</s>-kindled flame of fire — the tip of the fiery luminosity (<s>āgneya-dhāman</s>); that itself is the weapon (<s>astra</s>) because it protects from the rear (<s>astāt trāyate</s>). Or, the Lord who is without parts (<s>niṣkalanātha</s>) is here arisen; by that very [fire] ignited through the surge of the hiccup-like [breath], through the sequence of piercing the knots, from the piercing of the <s>Brahma</s>-knot (<s>brahmagranthi</s>). There, <s>prāṇa</s> is 'ha,' the weapon in the form of the flame of fire, etc. It fumigates (<s>dhūpayati</s>) the entire mass of objects of knowledge; it perfumes (<s>adhivāsayati</s>) everything with its own vibration — hence it is incense (<s>dhūpa</s>). //22//

children.text: anāhatā nadaty antar yā gaur dhāmni pare parā
children.translated_text: The unstruck (<s>anāhata</s>) [sound] that resonates within — the supreme <s>Cow</s> (<s>Gaur</s>, i.e. Sacred Speech) in the highest abode —

children.text: sā ghaṇṭā vādyate śambhor agre granthārthagarbhiṇī
children.translated_text: that bell (<s>ghaṇṭā</s>) is rung before <s>Śambhu</s> (the Auspicious One), pregnant with the meaning of the scriptures (<s>granthārtha</s>). [//23//]

body.text: Viv: aghaṃṭasiditi troṭayati iti aghaṇṭā parā prakṛṣṭā granthārthagarbhiṇī---antaritasakalavācyavācakakalāpā //23//
body.translated_text: Commentary (<s>Vivṛti</s>): '<s>aghaṇṭā</s>' — because she breaks apart (<s>troṭayati</s>) [all limitation, as in] '<s>aghaṃ ṭasid</s>' — <s>parā</s> (supreme), exalted, pregnant with the meaning of the scriptures — containing within herself the entire assemblage of the expressible and the expressive. //23//

children.translated_text: The flame of <s>Śakti</s> (power) blazing up from the fire at the root (<s>kandānala</s>), resembling the flame of a lamp —
I kindle it, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, for the dispelling of the darkness of delusion (<s>moha</s>). [//24//]

body.text: Viv: kandānalāt ādhāramadhyadhāmnaḥ ullasantī śaktiśikhā bindurūpā, tāṃ śāktasphāroddīpanāt dīparūpāṃ nādasūciśekharamudrānupraveśena uddīpayāmi //24//
body.translated_text: Commentary (<s>Vivṛti</s>): From the root-fire (<s>kandānala</s>), from the luminous center of the <s>ādhāra</s> [base <s>cakra</s>], the blazing <s>Śakti</s>-flame in the form of <s>bindu</s>; that [flame], through the kindling of the expansion of <s>Śakti</s>, in the form of a lamp — through the entry into the seal (<s>mudrā</s>) of the <s>nāda</s>-needle-crest, I kindle [it]. //24//

children.translated_text: The moon (<s>candra</s>) of the <s>kalā</s> (digit) of the nectar of the abandonment of mental modifications (<s>vṛttityāga</s>),

may it be a support (<s>samālambhana</s>) for the liberation of those who desire liberation (<s>mumukṣu</s>) — [this offering is] for the moon-crested one (<s>Candrakirīṭin</s>, <s>Śiva</s>). [//25-26//]

body.text: Viv: pramāṇaviparyayavikalpanidrāsmṛtivṛttiprahāṇapariśiṣṭatadanuprāṇakāvināśabodhaghanasārarūpaṃ samyag ālambhanaṃ samālambhanaṃ, sarvācchuraṇāt samālambhakaṃ vā tādṛśā eva hi mumukṣavo mucyante iti / tad uktam utpaladevapādaiḥ---

children.text: Q: yo 'vikalpam idam arthamaṇḍalaṃ & paśyatīśa nikhilaṃ bhavadvapuḥ /
children.translated_text: Quotation: 'He who sees this entire sphere of objects as non-conceptual, O Lord, as wholly your body,

children.text: Q: svātmapakṣaparipūrite jagaty & asya nityasukhinaḥ kuto bhayam // iti
children.translated_text: Quotation: in a world filled with his own self — whence could fear arise for such an eternally blissful one?' //

body.translated_text: Commentary (<s>Vivṛti</s>): Having abandoned the mental modifications — [those of] valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>), error (<s>viparyaya</s>), conceptualization (<s>vikalpa</s>), sleep (<s>nidrā</s>), and memory (<s>smṛti</s>) — what remains, the undestroyed vivifying [awareness], the dense essence of pure awakening (<s>bodha</s>) — that is the complete support (<s>samālambhana</s>), or, because it illuminates everything, it is the supporter (<s>samālambhaka</s>). Indeed, only those aspirants for liberation (<s>mumukṣu</s>) who are of such [nature] are liberated. As stated by the venerable <s>Utpaladeva</s>:

children.translated_text: The radiance (<s>dhāman</s>) arisen from the power of <s>nāda</s> (resonance), free from the three impurities (<s>malatrayam</s>),
may it be your crown (<s>uṣṇīṣa</s>), O <s>Rudra</s>, having shattered the bolt of the sky. [//26//]

body.text: Viv: nādaśakter bindūrdhvakalāyā uditam uparigataṃ nādāntatejovyapadeśyaṃ prakāśakatvād dhāma, tad eva avacchedahetunā āṇavādinā malatrayeṇa virahitam, tathā vidrāvitanabho 'rgalaṃ kṣapitaparavyomānuvedhanirodhakagranthicakram, uṣaṇe vikalpaploṣaṇe īśam uṣṇīṣam iti akṣarasāmyenāpi niruktiḥ //
body.translated_text: Commentary (<s>Vivṛti</s>): Arisen — gone above — from the power of <s>nāda</s> (the <s>kalā</s> above <s>bindu</s>), the radiance designated as the brilliance beyond <s>nāda</s>, because of its illuminating nature. That very [radiance], free from the three impurities (<s>mala</s>) — <s>āṇava</s> etc. — which are the causes of limitation. And having shattered the bolt of the sky — having destroyed the knot-wheel that obstructs the penetration of the supreme void (<s>paravyoman</s>). <s>Uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown) — because it is lord (<s>īśa</s>) of the burning (<s>uṣaṇa</s>) [away] of conceptual constructions — also by etymological resemblance of syllables. //

children.translated_text: Of the heart-ocean flooded with the essence of the nectar of devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) to you,
the radiantly arising lotus of <s>Brahman</s>, immaculate — may it be your crest-jewel (<s>śekhara</s>). [//27//]

body.text: Viv: anugrahaśaktirūpabhaktyamṛtavarṣāgādhīkṛtahṛtsamudrapratibhātabrahmapuṇḍarīkaṃ śikhāntaprāntakoṭyavabhāsanāt śekharam //27//
body.translated_text: Commentary (<s>Vivṛti</s>): The lotus of <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahmapuṇḍarīka</s>) reflected in the heart-ocean deepened by the rain of the nectar of devotion in the form of the grace-power (<s>anugrahaśakti</s>) — because of its manifesting at the edge of the tip of the crest (<s>śikhā</s>), [it is] the crest-jewel (<s>śekhara</s>). //27//

children.translated_text: The cluster of lotuses of awakening (<s>bodhāravinda</s>), O <s>Hara</s> (Destroyer), is your garland-chain (<s>hāralatā</s>);
and the eternally arisen <s>kalā</s> (digit) pervading the interior is your moon-digit (<s>candrakalā</s>). [//28-29//]

body.text: Viv: nānākārakaraṇeśvarīsamupahṛtaviṣayopahārahāralatāvatas tadaikyasamāpattimahākāśavyāptir evāhlādanadīptidhātvarthānugamāc candrakalā, taveti candrakamalamīlananayaḥ ko 'pi gurumukharahasyakrama uddīpitaḥ //29//
body.translated_text: Commentary (<s>Vivṛti</s>): The garland-chain consisting of sense-object offerings presented together by the various governing deities of the sense-organs (<s>karaṇeśvarī</s>); the pervasion of the great space (<s>mahākāśa</s>) through the absorption into the unity of those [offerings] is indeed the moon-digit, because of conformity to the verbal root-meanings of 'gladdening' (<s>āhlādana</s>) and 'shining' (<s>dīpti</s>). 'Your' (<s>tava</s>) — [this indicates] a certain secret method of [opening] the moon-lotus, revealed through the guru's mouth. //29//

children.translated_text: Having drawn forth with the solar rays of <s>Śakti</s> (power) from the lotus of the universal space,
savor the flow of the nectar of the consciousness-moon (<s>ciccandra</s>), O Lord of the World (<s>Jagatpati</s>). [//29//]

body.text: Viv: viśvākāśakuśeśayāt plāvakarasayuktyā akhilavigalanakrameṇa / tad uktaṃ mayā cakreśvarabhairavāṣṭake
body.translated_text: Commentary (<s>Vivṛti</s>): From the lotus of the universal space — by the method of the flooding [lunar] digit, through the sequence of the complete dissolution of everything. As stated by me in the <s>Cakreśvarabhairavāṣṭaka</s>:

children.translated_text: Quotation: 'The body-space, swollen by the swallowing of the fourfold elements, though exceedingly fierce,

children.text: Q: paramāṇuvatprahīṇaṃ & yatra nabhas tan numaḥ śaivam
children.translated_text: Quotation: [becomes] eliminated like an atom — we bow to that <s>Śaiva</s> space, where even the sky is dissolved.'

children.text: iti śaktair arkakarair mahākālasaṃkarṣiṇīkiraṇaiś cidrūpacandrapīyūṣarasacarvaṇena cinnabhaso 'pi u .........(lacuna)....... ṇatāpādanānantarasakaladhāmaghaṭṭanād ghorāghoraghasmararāvārāvavidrāvaṇacakrāticakrottaramahāsphāramayamahāmudrāvidrāvaṇānuttaraparaparispandasaundaryāvadyotanenāmāvasyāvāsanāvāsitaḥ ko 'pi saṃpradāya uṭṭaṅkitaḥ //29//
children.translated_text: [Continuation:] With the solar rays of <s>Śakti</s> — the rays of <s>Mahākālasaṃkarṣiṇī</s> (the Great Time-Attracting [goddess]) — through the savoring of the nectar-essence of the consciousness-form (<s>cidrūpa</s>) moon, even of the sky of consciousness [...lacuna...] through the striking of all radiant centers following that, through the transcendent great expansion (<s>mahāsphāra</s>) of the supreme great seal (<s>mahāmudrā</s>) that drives away the drive-awaying of the sounds of fierce and non-fierce devouring, through the revelation of the beauty of the supreme transcendent vibration — some lineage-tradition (<s>saṃpradāya</s>), perfumed by the fragrance of the new-moon-night (<s>amāvasyā</s>), is herein engraved. //29//

children.text: mantraṃ manasi tacchaktau tāṃ svadhāmni sadodite
children.translated_text: Having placed the <s>mantra</s> in the mind, that [mind] in <s>Śakti</s> (power), and her in the eternally arisen self-luminous abode (<s>svadhāman</s>),
I offer the proper practice of recitation (<s>japavidhi</s>) to <s>Śiva</s>. [//30//]

body.text: Viv: ``sahasro mānasa'' iti nītyā mantram anāhatasatatoccarad akulabhaṭṭārakākāram
body.translated_text: Commentary (<s>Vivṛti</s>): According to the rule 'a thousand [repetitions should be] mental,' the <s>mantra</s> — having the form of the Lord of <s>Akula</s> (<s>Akulabhaṭṭāraka</s>), continuously sounding in the unstruck [sound] (<s>anāhata</s>) —

body.text:
Q: ā gopālāṅganābālamlecchāḥ prākṛtabhāṣiṇaḥ
Q: antarjalacarāḥ satvās te 'pi nityaṃ bruvanti tam
body.translated_text: Quotation: 'From cowherds' wives to children to <s>mlecchas</s> — those who speak vernacular languages — and even creatures living underwater — they all constantly utter it.'

body.text: iti prāṇātmikakalāṃśāṃśikāsthitasamastatithiviṣuvadayanaparigamapūrapūritāśeṣajapaphalam ekoccāraviprasṛtākṣamālākṣamāloparigatādyantakarmaspandameruparyāvṛttidarśitasṛṣṭisaṃhāraṃ manasy avadhānamaye kṛtvā, tad api manaḥ prāptamantrasāmarasyaṃ śaktau prathanaprathamavīrye kṛtvā, śaktim api nijamahimani nityam aparityaktasārvātmyasarvottīrṇatātirekamahodaye sarvavarṇānāṃ śaktikramasphuritatattatsvarūpānuprāṇanena svarūpalābhāt / tad uktaṃ
body.translated_text: Thus, having established in the mind attentive awareness — whose fruit of complete <s>japa</s> (recitation) encompasses all <s>tithis</s> (lunar days), equinoxes, solstices, passages and fullnesses situated in the parts and sub-parts of the <s>kalā</s> (phase) whose nature is <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), and which displays creation and dissolution through the revolution around <s>Meru</s> [at the summit] of the rosary (<s>akṣamālā</s>) — with the beginning and ending impulse of action traversed by the rosary of letters emitted in a single utterance — and having then [placed] that mind, which has attained unity with the <s>mantra</s>, into <s>Śakti</s> (Power) whose primordial potency is manifestation; and [having placed] <s>Śakti</s> too into her own supreme glory — the ever-unabandoned, all-transcending, surpassingly effulgent state of universal selfhood — [where there is] attainment of one's own true nature through the vivification of each and every essential form as manifested by the successive unfolding of <s>Śakti</s> in all the phonemes. As it is said:

body.text: Q: tad ākramya balaṃ mantrāḥ
body.translated_text: [Quotation:] 'Mantras, having mounted upon that power...'

body.text: iti / evaṃvidhaṃ japamakaraṇakaraṇena nirvartya, śivāya svātmamaheśvare tādarthyena viśeṣeṇa niravaśeṣaṃ buddhye samyak, ityevaṃvidhamahāvīryasphārasāmarasyamayasatatoditajapāvadhānātirekeṇa paśūnāṃ japa uccaritapradhvaṃsivarṇanirvartyaḥ, etat paramārthatāyām api nirvīryabījatayā na samyaksiddhisādhanabhāvam aśnuta ity uktaṃ bhavati //30//
body.translated_text: Thus. Having accomplished this kind of <s>japa</s> through the method of non-doing-as-doing, 'for <s>Śiva</s>' — I understand fully, with the specific purpose of [offering to] the great Lord who is one's own Self, completely and without remainder. Thus it is stated that the <s>japa</s> of bound souls (<s>paśus</s>), accomplished through uttered and immediately destroyed phonemes, even when it has the highest truth as its [intended] object, does not attain the status of being a means to complete <s>siddhi</s> (perfection), due to [the phonemes] being seeds devoid of potency. //30//

children.translated_text: In the complete renunciation of all objects, or in their acceptance, with infinite [capacity] —

children.text: anābilaṃ parāṃ vyāptiṃ mudrāṃ badhnāmi dhūrjaṭe
children.translated_text: I bind the supreme <s>mudrā</s> (seal) of all-pervading, unclouded [awareness], O <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s> (Śiva)!

body.text: Viv: dhunoti sarvaṃ, raṃhati sarvatra, janayati sarvaṃ, ṭīkate sarvatra iti āgūritākramacatuṣṭayārtho dhūrjaṭiḥ / etāṃ layodayamudrām ekām api pañcadhā vakṣyamāṇanayena sphurantīṃ badhnāmy ātmasātkaromi / akhilārthaparihāre vā svīkāre vā askhalanāt aparicchinnamahiman? vedyavedakakālikābhir akaluṣitām, akṛtrimamahāvyāptimayīm / iyam eva cāntarlakṣyabahirdṛṣṭibhāvena tyāgagrahābhyāṃ bhairavī, akhilāsvādacamatkārasphuraṇābhyām api tyāgagrahavigrahā lelihānā, sarvaparikṣapaṇena ca svāvaśeṣamātreṇāpi tyāgagrahātmikaivakaraṅkiṇī, svarūpākṣamatāyām api tadgrāsagṛdhnusphurattāsāraiva tadrūpaiva krodhinī, paravyomni vyāptyunmimiṣāsaṃjihīrṣātmakollāsopaśamasîdhyaiva khe caratīti khecarī ity etallakṣaṇalakṣitatayaiva sarvamudrîṇîm iyam ekaiva pañcadhî prasarantī tattadvacanabhedaiś carvyate ca //31//
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s> — [etymologically:] He who shakes (<s>dhunoti</s>) everything, who rushes (<s>raṃhati</s>) everywhere, who generates (<s>janayati</s>) everything, who establishes (<s>ṭīkate</s>) everywhere — thus <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s> [is explained] through the four-fold meaning derived by sequence of syllables. This one <s>mudrā</s> of dissolution and emergence, though single, I bind — i.e., make my own — as it flashes forth in five ways according to the method to be explained. In the relinquishment or acceptance of all objects, without faltering, of unlimited glory, unstained by the temporal divisions of knower and known, consisting of genuine and spontaneous great all-pervasion. And this very [mudrā], through the mode of inner-focus-with-outward-gaze, is <s>Bhairavī</s> [mudrā] through renunciation and acceptance; through the flashing forth of the relish and wonder of all [experience], it is <s>Lelihānā</s> [mudrā], whose body is renunciation and acceptance; through the complete consumption [of all] leaving only the residue of oneself, it is <s>Karaṅkiṇī</s> [mudrā], consisting of renunciation and acceptance; even in the incapacity [to grasp] one's own true nature, the flashing forth that hungrily devours that [very incapacity] — being of that very nature — is <s>Krodhinī</s> [mudrā]; through the <s>siddhi</s> of the subsidence of the expansion-impulse of the desire-to-pervade and the desire-to-withdraw in the supreme sky (<s>paravyoman</s>), [the mudrā that] moves in the sky is <s>Khecarī</s> [mudrā]. This single [mudrā], characterized by these very marks, extending in five ways as the essence of all <s>mudrās</s>, is elaborated through the various textual distinctions. //31//

children.translated_text: Having bound [the awareness] in the two ear-cavities (<s>śaṣkulī-karṇa</s>), the sound that reverberates therein —
that is Your song (<s>gīta</s>); and Your instrumental music (<s>vādya</s>) [arises] from the striking of the primal pair [of channels].

body.text: Viv: śrotrapuṭikayor yo 'ntarninadann iva sāmānyasvarūpo yo 'sau, gītaṃ sa eva, ādyakandobhayapakṣasaṃkocāt nānānāḍīveṇuvane vicarann upajanitatataghanasuṣiratāramandramadhyamabhedāṅkuritakalāprastārāstṛtacañcatpuṭacāṣapuṭapañcapāṇipramukhamukharataratārabhedo vādyabhāvam bhajate / ``śaṣkulīkarṇayor antar'' iti vā pāṭhaḥ --- golakatacchaktyor antar ityarthaḥ / gopya iti pāṭhe bhagavata āmantraṇaṃ svaprakāsatvās ananyaprakāsya! ityarthaḥ, śaṣkulīkarṇayor ādyasaṃpuṭaghaṭṭanād yo rāvas tad gītam iti anvīyate //32//
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] The generic essential nature that resonates within the two ear-cups — that itself is the song (<s>gīta</s>). From the contraction of both sides of the primal cavity, [the sound], wandering through the reed-forest of the various <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels), generates tones differentiated as deep, dense, piercing, low, medium, and high — sprouted from the unfolding of <s>kalās</s> (phases) — [producing] the variety of rhythmic clapping sounds prominent among the five [prāṇas] — this assumes the nature of instrumental music (<s>vādya</s>). Or the reading is 'within the two ear-shells' — meaning within the spherical structures and their <s>śaktis</s>. In the reading '<s>gopya</s>' (O secret one), it is an address to the Lord: 'O Self-luminous one who is not illuminated by anything else!' — this is the meaning. The construction is: 'The sound that [arises] from the striking of the primal pair in the two ear-cavities — that is the song.' //32//

children.translated_text: Through the immersion in the <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic flavor) of Your state of being, uplifted by the splendor of the <s>tāṇḍava</s> (cosmic dance),

children.text: mantrādhvani nadāmy antaḥ kim u bāhyārthabhāvanaiḥ
children.translated_text: I roar within on the path of <s>mantra</s> — what need then of external conceptualizations?

body.text: Viv: tvanmayotkarṣeṣu śṛṅgārādiṣv api raseṣv āveśāt tvadanukārivikīrṇanijamarīcimayakarakalpitasaṃkīrṇāsaṃkīrṇapatākādisamudbodhitabhāvavaibhavābhinayo bhavābhavodghaṭṭanavighaṭṭanajavanikāprāveśanirgamanākampitasvarūpo 'pi nṛttam ārabhe, tad uktaṃ mayā śivarātrivicāravārtike
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Through immersion in the <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic sentiments) — <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (love) and the others — even in Your exalted [states], the dramatic expression (<s>abhinaya</s>) of emotional splendor, awakened through the established and non-established <s>patākā</s> (dramatic gestures) etc., fashioned by the rays of one's own scattered [awareness] emulating You — and with one's own essential nature shaken by the entering and exiting through the curtain of the arising and dissolution of existence and non-existence — I commence the dance. As I have stated in my <s>Śivarātrivicāravārttika</s>:

children.translated_text: [Quotation:] 'The ever-assumed successive unfoldings of the faculties, flashing [with consciousness], | established in hundreds of wondrous emotional states —'
[Quotation:] 'Actionless, I cause my own ray-dancers to dance, | I who am the master-choreographer of the supreme dance.' //

body.text: [Śivarātrivicāravārtika of Ramyadeva]

iti / mantrādhvani dhvanidhāmani guptabhāṣaṇapravaṇapaśyantīpade, yad vā vācyavācakādhvaṣaṭkamadhyavartipañcamantramahimani, nadāmi cidbhairavaikaghanatāpramodena garjāmi / kiṃ varākair bāhyaviṣayavikalpātaṅkaiḥ, iti pararasaparitṛptimahodgāraṃ prakaṭayati ``na māmy antaḥ kim u bāhye 'tra bhauvane'' iti vā pāṭhaḥ, tatra na māmi na varte kim u bhauvane kalādāv akalānte bhuvanādhvanītyarthaḥ //33//
body.translated_text: Thus. 'On the path of <s>mantra</s>' — in the abode of resonance (<s>dhvani-dhāman</s>), in the stage of <s>Paśyantī</s> (the 'seeing' level of speech), inclined toward hidden discourse; or alternatively, in the glory of the five <s>mantras</s> situated in the middle of the sixfold path of the signified and the signifier. 'I roar' — I thunder with the delight of the one-pointed density of <s>cit-bhairava</s> (consciousness-as-<s>Bhairava</s>). What [use are] the pitiful anxieties of external object-conceptualizations? — thus he reveals the great outpouring of the supreme satisfaction of transcendent <s>rasa</s>. Or the reading is: 'I do not exist within — what to speak of externally, in this world.' In that [reading]: 'I do not exist,' meaning I do not abide — what to speak of in the <s>bhuvanādhvan</s> (cosmic path of worlds), [extending] from <s>kalā</s> to the end of <s>kalā</s>. //33//

children.translated_text: The sky of the meditation on <s>Śiva</s>-hood, in the form of an unbroken circle (<s>maṇḍala</s>) —
this canopy (<s>vitāna</s>) has been fashioned by me above, for <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva).

body.text: Viv: vitanoti sarvaṃ vitanyate vā sarvatra iti vitānam //34//
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] <s>Vitāna</s> — that which spreads (<s>vitanoti</s>) everything, or which is spread (<s>vitanyate</s>) everywhere. //34//

children.translated_text: Having drawn forth from the sky of the heart, through the channel [of <s>suṣumnā</s>], the circle of radiance,
it is held before <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s> (Śiva) like a beautiful <s>cāmara</s> (fly-whisk), by me.

body.text: Viv: prabuddhakuṇḍalinīspaṣṭībhāvabhāsuramadhyamadhāmadaṇḍānupreraṇaprayatnaprasṛtabrahmabilotkālitabaindhavadīptivṛndaṃ hṛdayagaganaprasṛtaṃ trividhatāpahāritayā cāmaraṃ dhārayāmi //35//
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] The multitude of <s>bindu</s>-radiance, ejected through the opening of <s>Brahma-bila</s> (the aperture at the crown), propelled by the effort of impelling [the breath] through the middle channel (<s>madhyama-dhāman</s>) — the staff resplendent with the manifestation of the awakened <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s> — [this radiance,] emanating from the sky of the heart, I hold as a <s>cāmara</s> (fly-whisk) that removes the threefold suffering. //35//

children.translated_text: With the <s>haṃsa</s>-breaths (<s>prāṇa</s>-winds), released from and entering the tip of the nose's nostril-hut,
You are fanned, O Lord, as if by <s>tālavṛnta</s> (palm-leaf fans) extending before [You].

body.text: Viv: visṛtaiḥ praviṣṭaiḥ, prasṛtaiḥ, haṃsamārutaiḥ prāṇapavanais tāluvṛntair ivotkṣepakatulyaiḥ //36//
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Released' means entered; 'extending' [means flowing forth]; 'by <s>haṃsa</s>-winds' means by the <s>prāṇa</s> breezes; 'by palm-fans' means by [instruments] comparable to fans. //36//

children.translated_text: Free from all affliction, | cooled by the nectar of devotion to You —
this parasol (<s>ātapatram</s>) is held by us | for You, O Great-souled One.

body.text: Viv: viṣayāsaṅgakalilarahitaṃ, tvanmayatāmṛtavimalaṃ chatraṃ dhāryate //37//
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Free from the turbidity of attachment to sense-objects, pure with the nectar of oneness with You — the parasol is held. //37//

children.translated_text: Through the abandonment of the stable of possessiveness (<s>mamatā</s>), | capable of attracting the three worlds,
the steed of ego-sense (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>) | is prepared as Your mount (<s>vāhana</s>).

body.text: Viv: bhavanirāvaraṇavijayayātropakrame niyatāhantāmamatāparikṣaye pūrṇāhantātmako 'haṅkāro hayas tvadativahanāya //38//
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] At the commencement of the victory-march for the conquest that removes all coverings of worldly existence, through the destruction of the limited 'I-ness' (<s>ahantā</s>) and 'mine-ness' (<s>mamatā</s>), the ego-sense that consists of the full 'I-ness' [of universal consciousness] becomes the steed for carrying You forth. //38//

children.translated_text: Radiant with the <s>nāgavallī</s> (betel) leaf | from the <s>Nandana</s> garden of the bliss of self-awareness,
fragrant with the flashing impulse-moon — | this <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel offering) is presented to You.

body.text: Viv: tāmbūlaṃ---tāmrabhavāmūlam, akhiloparañjakatvāt, nijabodhānandanandanodyānapraphullo, nāgaḥ śarīraḥ pavanaviśeṣas tasya vallī prathamaprāṇodbhedaśaktiḥ tatsaṃpattikāsundaram, udgacchadādyecchācimicimikākarpūravāsitā---ubhayor api sarvacamatkārakatvāt //39//
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] <s>Tāmbūla</s> — [etymologically:] having a reddish (<s>tāmra</s>) origin (<s>mūla</s>), because it colors everything. Blossoming in the pleasure-garden of the bliss of one's own awakening, the <s>nāga</s> (serpent/body) — the particular wind of the body — its <s>vallī</s> (creeper) is the <s>Śakti</s> of the first bursting forth of <s>prāṇa</s> — beautiful with the wealth of that [prāṇa]. Scented with the camphor of the initial sparkling flashes of the primordial will (<s>icchā</s>) that rises up — because both [elements] produce universal wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>). //39//

children.translated_text: The accumulated fuel of impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) | born from the distinction of enjoyer and enjoyed —

children.text: advaitāgnau juhomy antaḥ & śāṃkare sreyasām nidhau
children.translated_text: I offer [this] internally into the fire of non-duality (<s>advaita</s>), | in [the abode of] <s>Śaṅkara</s> (Śiva), the treasury of all blessings.

body.text: Viv: bhogyabhoktṛvibhāgatadudgatavāsanādāruvisaram avibhāgaśambhudhāmni sāmarasyaṃ lambhayāmi //40//
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] The mass of impression-fuel born from the division of enjoyer and enjoyed — I bring into unity (<s>sāmarasya</s>) in the undifferentiated abode of <s>Śambhu</s>. //40//

children.translated_text: Grasping with the two hands of Illumination (<s>prakāśa</s>) and Space (<s>ākāśa</s>) | the ladle of the <s>unmanā</s> (transcendent mind),
filled with the dripping oil of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> — | I make oblation into the fire, O Unborn One.

body.text: Viv: aje sarvādisiddhe pūrvodite śivadhāmahavyabhuji grāhyagrāhakabhedavāsanendhanadahanasamedhite svarasavigalitapriyāpriyaphaladharmādharanibaddhavāsanāghṛtapūrṇāhutiṃ juhomy avimarśatadvirāmarūpasamanonmanāpāṇibhyāṃ sūkṣmakaraṇaśaktitaduparamāṅgulipañcakopaśobhitābhyāṃ taduparivartanād ``unmanyante paraḥ śivaḥ'' iti dṛśā unmanāsrucaṃ parigṛhya pūrṇāṃ juhomi, iti saṃkṣayapradhānāyām api vṛttāv aviluptam eva pāripūrṇyam---iti pūrnakṛśadevataikātmyamayah ko 'pi nayaḥ prathitaḥ / uktaṃ ca mayaivākulakālikātriṃśikāyāṃ---
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] In the Unborn — the fire of the <s>Śiva</s>-abode established at the primordial beginning, the receiver of oblations — which is kindled by the fuel of the impressions of the distinction of grasper and grasped, I offer the full oblation filled with the ghee of the impressions bound to pleasant and unpleasant fruits — [the impressions of] <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> that flow down by their own nature — [grasping] with the two hands of reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>) and its repose, which are the <s>unmanā</s> (transcendent mind), adorned with the five fingers of subtle power and its cessation — and due to its turning upward, [one sees that] 'beyond <s>unmanī</s> is Supreme <s>Śiva</s>' — grasping the <s>unmanā</s>-ladle, I offer the full [oblation]. Thus even in the activity (<s>vṛtti</s>) where dissolution predominates, fullness (<s>pāripūrṇya</s>) is never lost — thus is revealed a certain method [that establishes] identity between the full and the emaciated deity. As I myself have stated in the <s>Akulakālikātriṃśikā</s>:

body.text:
Q: svānandatas tribhuvanaṃ kavalaṃ vidhāya & svātmānam apy atitarāṃ samadā grasantī
Q: tṛptā tathāpy aparikhaṇḍitanityasiddha&svātantryapūrṇavibhavā kṛśamūrtir avyāt
body.translated_text: [Quotation:] 'Having made the three worlds a morsel from her own bliss, | swallowing even her own self with extreme relish, | yet satisfied — of ever-established, unbroken, free, | and full sovereignty — may the Emaciated One protect [us]!'

children.translated_text: Illuminated by the rays of the moon | that is the lord of the night of meditation upon You,
may my mind-gem (<s>citta-cintāmaṇi</s>) | serve Your inner worship (<s>antarmāna</s>).

body.text: Viv: bāhyavyāvṛttivigamapūrvakam antarmananam anantatayā sphuraṇam antarmānaṃ tadvidhau, tvadanubhavaśaśiprakāśavivaśīkṛtaḥ, cittam eva cintāmaṇir bhavatsamāveśena tadvad eva saṃkalpamātreṇa sarvasamullāsāt //42//
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] The inner contemplation (<s>antarmānana</s>) — the flashing forth as infinite [awareness] preceded by the cessation of outward orientation — in the rite of that [contemplation], [the mind is] overpowered by the moonlight of the experience of You. The <s>citta</s> (mind) itself becomes a <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling jewel), since through immersion in You, like that [gem], by mere intention (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) it manifests everything. //42//

children.translated_text: Placing [my offering], refined, into the lotus-cup | of the hand of <s>Mokṣalakṣmī</s> (the Goddess of Liberation),
I present [it], O <s>Bhagavan</s> (Lord), | as the sacrificial fee (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) consisting of the entirety of my vital breath.

body.text: Viv: prāṇā eva teṣāṃ vā sarvasvam āṇavaṃ svarūpaṃ, tan nivedayāmi---māyīyapārimityābhāsanirāsasamupalabdhasatatasiddhaparapāripūrṇyabṛṃhitatayā niḥśeṣato vedayāmi / mokṣalakṣmyā bhavaunmukhyaparāvṛttāyāḥ saṃviddevyāḥ karāmbhasi paramavīciniḥṣyande jātaṃ yat pātram pātatrāṇātmakam aviluptam avadhānaṃ, tadarpitaṃ kṛtvā, saṃskṛtāṃ kṛtaśāstrācāryasaṃpradāyopaskarām / tad evaṃ māyopakalpitatattadavacchedavicchedikramākramacakracāramahāsāmarasyasamāpattipratipādanena yad eva ``namaḥ sūryakalā'' ityādinā prakrāntaṃ tad eva paryavasitam //43//
body.translated_text: [Commentary on v.43:] The vital breaths (<s>prāṇas</s>) themselves, or rather, their totality is the innate (<s>āṇava</s>) essential nature — that I offer: I know it completely, as nourished by the supreme fullness (<s>parapāripūrṇya</s>) realized through the removal of the appearance of <s>māyīya</s> (illusory) limitation, perpetually established. Having made the offering placed in the vessel — which is the unwavering attention, an indestructible [receptacle of] protection, born in the supreme wave-flow of the stream from the hand-lotus of the Goddess of Consciousness (<s>saṃviddevī</s>), who has turned away from the orientation toward worldly existence toward the splendor of liberation — [the offering being] refined, endowed with the traditional transmission of scripture, teacher, and lineage (<s>śāstrācāryasaṃpradāya</s>). Thus, through the demonstration of the great equipoise (<s>mahāsāmarasya</s>) — the attainment of the wheel-movement (<s>cakracāra</s>) of sequential and non-sequential cutting of the various delimitations superimposed by <s>māyā</s> — what was commenced with 'Homage to the rays of the sun' etc. is hereby concluded. //43//

children.translated_text: The good, who wish to cross to the further shore

of the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), should take refuge on high in the boat of the worship of inner devotion (<s>bhāvapūjā</s>) of the Moon-Crested One (<s>Candramauli</s>, i.e., Śiva).

body.text: Viv: śrayantv avadhānena sevantāṃ, bhāvapūjāmayaṃ taraṇḍakaṃ potam //44//
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Let them take refuge — let them attend to — the boat (<s>taraṇḍaka</s>) consisting of the worship of inner devotion (<s>bhāvapūjā</s>). //44//

children.translated_text: Thus, whatever merit has been acquired through

children.text: śreyas tena jagat kṛtsnaṃ & dveṣadoṣād vimucyatām
children.translated_text: the bowing at the feet of <s>Īśāna</s> (the Lord, Śiva) — by that, may the entire world be freed from the fault of hatred!

body.text: Viv: niyatadarśanāvagrahagrahasamudgatadarśanāntaranirbhartsanākhaṇḍanasamayalopāj jagad vimuktam astu, niyatadarśanahevākitā hi sarvodayaviśrāmabhūmibhūtaparatattvaparikhaṇḍanatvāmastvāt sarvasyaiva paraḥ prakāraḥ / tad uktam mayā kṛtāntatāntiśāntistave---
