body.translated_text: [Commentary:] May the world be freed from the loss [incurred] at the time of the shattering and cutting of the reproach of all other doctrines arising from the seizure of fixed dogmatic adherence to a particular viewpoint — for the commitment to a fixed viewpoint, being the nature of the fragmenting of the Supreme Reality which is the resting-ground of the arising of all, is indeed the highest mode of everything. As I have stated in my <s>Kṛtāntatāntiśāntistava</s> —

children.text: Q: māyeyaṃ bahurūpatām upagatā nānā yathā te vibho & vidyāpy evam anantabhedagahanā no cet kathaṃ syād idam /
children.translated_text: [Quote:] 'This <s>māyā</s> has assumed manifold forms; O Lord, just as Your [power], so too <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) is dense with infinite divisions — were it not so, how could this [world] be?'

children.text: Q: naiḥsvābhāvyagamena ke cana pare vaiviktyataḥ ke 'pi vā & sārvātmyena pare taduttaradṛśā muktāḥ pare sarvatah //
children.translated_text: [Quote:] 'Some [are liberated] through the path of essencelessness (<s>naiḥsvābhāvya</s>), others through distinctness (<s>vaiviktya</s>), others through universality (<s>sārvātmya</s>), and others, with the vision transcending that, [are] liberated from all.'

body.text: iti / advayadvādaśikāyām api---
body.translated_text: Thus. And in the <s>Advayadvādaśikā</s> also —

children.text: Q: yady atattvaparihārapūrvakaṃ & tattvam eṣi tad atattvam eva hi /
children.translated_text: [Quote:] 'If you seek the Real (<s>tattva</s>) through the prior elimination of the unreal (<s>atattva</s>), that is indeed the unreal!'

children.text: Q: yady atattvam atha tattvam eva vā & tattvam eva nanu tattvam īdṛśam //
children.translated_text: [Quote:] 'If [you call it] unreal, it is nonetheless the Real — the Real is surely of such a nature as this!' //
Accept this hymn, O <s>Parameśvara</s> (Supreme Lord), Witness of the Universe! — from one whose mental activity has abandoned the concerns of honor and dishonor,
who is intoxicated [with devotion], whose crest is absorbed at the pedestal of Your pair of feet, whose body is covered in ashes, who holds a skull (<s>nṛkapāla</s>) in his hand.

body.text: Viv: viśvasya sākṣī viśvarūpo vāmantryate, mānāvamānayoḥ grahaṇāgrahaṇayor niṣprapañcaprapañcayor mamatayojjhitā cittavṛttir yasya tadyuktā vā tyaktā cittavṛttir yena, aṃhaḥ pāpaṃ haratīti, ahaṃkṛd eva vāṅghris tadyugam anāvaraṇajñānakriyārūpaṃ tasya pīṭhaṃ paramaśivarūpaṃ tatra nilīnamauleḥ praśāntakaraṇapañcakakañcukopacayaploṣapariśiṣṭena ākhilabhūtihetunā avabodhabhūtivibhavena avaguṇṭhitā ācchāditās tanavo mitatayā sphurantaḥ sarvabhāvā yena, nuḥ aṇor yat kapālaṃ, kaṃ mahāsvātantryarūpam anavacchinnaṃ brahma pālayati gopayatīti nṛkapālaṃ karparaṃ tat pāṇau ekasmin udbubhūṣāmarīcilakṣaṇe mitatayā iyattayā tulitaṃ yasya sa tathoktaḥ //46//
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] He is addressed as 'Witness of the Universe' or as 'having the form of the Universe' (<s>viśvarūpa</s>). One whose mental activity has been abandoned with respect to honor and dishonor, grasping and non-grasping, the manifest and the un-elaborated — or: one who has abandoned mental activity. <s>Aṃhas</s> means sin, which he destroys — thus the ego itself is the 'foot' (<s>aṅghri</s>); the pair of those, having the form of unobstructed knowledge and action — their pedestal (<s>pīṭha</s>) is the form of <s>Paramaśiva</s> (Supreme Śiva); in that, his crest is absorbed. [He whose] bodies — the various phenomena shining forth in limited form — are enveloped, i.e., covered, by the splendor of awakening (<s>avabodha</s>), the cause of all prosperity, remaining after the burning of the accumulation of the five sheaths (<s>kañcuka</s>) of the pacified sense-faculties. <s>Nṛkapāla</s> (human skull) means the skull (<s>karpara</s>) that protects (<s>pālayati</s>) <s>ka</s>, i.e., the unconditioned <s>Brahman</s> of the form of supreme freedom — this is held in one hand, characterized by the ray of the desire to manifest forth, weighed [as if balanced] in its limited measure — thus is he described. //46//

children.translated_text: In the great garden of <s>Pāśupata</s> [doctrine], a certain ascetic (<s>tāpasa</s>), having rested,
composed the supreme worship of inner devotion (<s>bhāvanuti</s>) to <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva), the Lord of the Consciousness-Wheel (<s>Ciccakranātha</s>).

body.text: Viv: ``nirastaśāstrārthavikalpajālā & devyāḥ śmaśāne karavīrakākhye'' iti dṛśā bhasmaśabdavyākhyānavarṇitasvarūpe mahāpāśupatodyāne, bhairavāṇāṃ paśūnāṃ patir akalitaciccakreśvarātmakas tadudyāne tadūrdhvayāne sarvātiśāyini, viśramya ananyatayā pratiṣṭhāṃ prāpya, ata eva kaś cid ajñāyamānapaśuparikalpitaniyatasaṃjñāvacchedaḥ, mahati tapasi citsamāveśamaye bhavaḥs tāpasaḥ ciccakranāthasya---
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] In the great garden of <s>Pāśupata</s> — whose essential nature has been described in the explanation of the word '<s>bhasma</s>' (ash) through the vision [expressed in the verse] 'In the cremation ground called <s>Karavīraka</s>, of the Goddess, free from the net of conceptual elaboration of scriptural meanings' — the Lord of the <s>Paśus</s> (bound souls), <s>Bhairava</s>, whose essence is the Lord of the Consciousness-Wheel (<s>Ciccakreśvara</s>) — in His garden, i.e., in His supreme transcendence surpassing all. Having rested, i.e., having attained firm establishment through non-otherness. Therefore, 'a certain one' — whose designation and delimitation, imagined by the unknowing bound souls, [is unknown]. A <s>tāpasa</s> (ascetic), in whom exists (<s>bhavaḥ</s>) the great <s>tapas</s> (austerity) consisting of the immersion in consciousness (<s>citsamāveśa</s>). [He composed the worship] of <s>Śambhu</s>, the Lord of the Consciousness-Wheel (<s>Ciccakranātha</s>), whose essential nature has been described by <s>Rājānaka Utpaladeva</s> beginning with —

children.translated_text: [Quote:] 'To Him who is the resting-ground undivided from all the diverse streams of universal consciousness (<s>saṃvid</s>),
[Quote:] homage to <s>Śiva</s>, the ocean of <s>caitanya</s> (consciousness), whose body is the [universal] knowing subject (<s>pramātṛ</s>)!' //

body.text: ityādinā rājānakotpaladevanirvarṇitasvarūpasya śambhoḥ śreyaḥprabhavasya bhāvena sarvabhāvaikyasamāpattisamāveśamayena nutiṃ parāṃ cakre, iti cakranātha+cakre+śabdābhyām ātmanaś cakrapāṇināma dyotayati //47//
body.translated_text: — [of that <s>Śambhu</s>], the source of supreme good (<s>śreyas</s>), he composed the supreme worship (<s>nuti</s>) through inner devotion (<s>bhāva</s>), i.e., through the immersion in the equipoise of unity with all states of being (<s>sarvabhāvaikyasamāpattisamāveśa</s>). And by the words 'Cakranātha' and 'cakre' (he made), he indicates his own name '<s>Cakrapāṇi</s>.' //47//

children.translated_text: I bow to the lineage of teachers (<s>gurukrama</s>), [whose forms are] unseen, arrived [through grace],
an expanse of the wheel of rays (<s>marīcicakra</s>), whose sole cause is grace (<s>anugraha</s>). //

[Colophon:] <s>Ramyadeva</s>, a twice-born, born with the illuminated instruction of the true secret [teaching] conducive to the breaking of the toil of birth and other [afflictions], filled with boundless enthusiasm and joy generated by the command illuminated by the feet of the Goddess <s>Pīṭheśī</s>, [who appeared] from the mouth of the best of <s>dvijas</s> (twice-born) named <s>Yogānanda</s>,

children.text: stotre bhāvopahāre vivaraṇam akarod ramyadevo dvijanmā &janmādyāyāsabhaṅgapravaṇamatilasatsadrahasyopadeśaḥ //
children.translated_text: composed the commentary (<s>vivaraṇa</s>) on this <s>Bhāvopahāra</s> hymn. //
